newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile supermarket sales rise five pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile supermarket sales rise five pct in 1996.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales rose five percent last year compared with 1995, although sales in December fell 4.2 percent against the same month 1995, said the Association of Chilean Supermarkets.
"This rise (in 1995) is within a period of restricted economic growth which has hurt all trade and supermarkets in particular," said the association in a statement.
Supermarkets, which account for most of Chile's domestic shopping, reported sales totalling $2.9 billion last year, it said.

Sales fell 4.2 percent in real terms last month compared with December 1995 in part as a result of the Central Bank's restrictive monetary policy whose full effect was felt in the second half of last year.
The association said it expects sales to grow six percent this year, reaching just over $3 billion.
Sales are seen growing only moderately until mid-year but then could take off if the bank carries out a widely-expected interest rate cut in the first half of the year.
The bank has raised rates twice in the last year to curb booming consumer spending which had fuelled Chile's robust economic growth in 1995 and early 1996.
Chileans are Latin America's most enthusiastic supermarket shoppers and supermaket sales are widely regarded as a barometer of overall consumer spending.
